_readme: Single source of truth for CHANNEL STATE and DECISION DATES.
Written 31 Jul 2026 after the Boris Cherny / YC talk 'Delete Your CLAUDE.md'.
Rule: anything that CHANGES lives here. Prose files (OPERATING-NOTES) keep only
timeless, counterintuitive lessons. Task prompts must READ this, never restate it.
Why: on 30-31 Jul the same fact (IG paused, TikTok paused, Meta token revoked) was
copied into 4+ task prompts and 2 python files. When TikTok was dropped, post_guard
and the daily card still asked for it -- the exact drift that caused the 4-day
blackout, just in a different file. One fact, one place.

kind = which pipeline a channel belongs to. Added 31 Jul after a dry-run of the daily card rule (state != paused AND auto == false) pulled PANTIP into the VIDEO card - pantip is a forum-comment flow with its own approval path, not a clip upload. Selection rules must filter on kind, never on state alone.

That was a July figure nobody ever refreshed, so the guard was judging against a number that had quietly stopped being true. Left null on purpose: the heartbeat now reports raw view counts instead of scoring them, and will only score again once someone sets a figure here with a date.

tiktok.reason: Not restricted, just not working. 37 posts bought no audience and no measurable traffic. Retired rather than paused because 'paused pending evidence' is what it has been since 20 Jul and the evidence is now in.
tiktok.evidence: Read TikTok Studio in the browser on 7 Aug - it does NOT need the owner's phone, which is why this sat open for 8 days. 37 posts live, 0 drafts, EVERY post privacy = public, no warning banner anywhere in Studio. So the account is NOT restricted and NOT shadowbanned - the theory that held this decision open was simply wrong. What is true: 12 followers, 1-2 views per post, 9 video views in the last 7 days, 0 profile views, 0 comments, 0 shares, and 0 sessions to the site ever. Last post 26 Jul; batch3 sent it nothing at all (0/7). The clips it did get were 10s, unlike the 20-21s used elsewhere.
tiktok.reversible: Set state back to 'testing' and give it a real run: same clips as the other channels, not 10s cut-downs, for 14 consecutive days. Anything less repeats a test that was never run.

gates.note: Phase 1 ran 17-30 Jul (reply-only, <=3/week, no brand/link). From 31 Jul the daily task may still find+draft but must NOT recommend posting until the owner rules on phase 2. ADDED HERE 31 Jul 2026 by watchdog: this date previously existed ONLY in Claude/Scheduled/pantip-daily-opportunity/SKILL.md, so the expiry sweep - which reads this gates[] array - was blind to it. The SKILL.md ordered a warning on every run from 29 Jul, but the task was disabled 26-30 Jul in the token-saving sweep, so the warning was never delivered even once. Same one-truth-many-places drift as the 27-30 Jul blackout.
gates.decision: do NOT open phase 2 yet - extend phase 1 (reply-only, <=3/week, spaced) to 14 Aug
gates.rationale: Phase 2 means starting NEW threads, which is the highest-risk action available on an account that is one strike from a permanent ban. The precondition for phase 2 was a clean, visible 30-day history - but we barely used phase 1: last Pantip post 26 Jul, 0/3 used this week. A thin record is not the same as a clean record, and it is the record a moderator would read. Extending reply-only costs almost nothing and builds the exact evidence phase 2 requires.

gates.task: owner decision - which posting cap governs
decides: posts per day per channel (1 or 2)
gates.note: Two rules disagree and both are live. POSTING-POLICY_antispam_20260702.md rule 2 says <=2/day/channel; STANDING-RULE_autopost.md (18 Jul, owner instruction, and until 31 Jul NOT even committed to git) says 1/day/channel. For Threads the owner then approved 2/day explicitly on 19 Jul, which post-dates the standing rule - so 2 clearly governs there. For Facebook nothing resolves it: the live guard (fb-evening-safetynet) enforces 2. policy.limits.posts_per_day.default is therefore set to 2 = what the system actually enforces today, NOT a ruling. Found 31 Jul 2026 while auditing my own breach of 3 FB posts in 20 minutes - which is over BOTH caps either way.
gates.decision: cap stays 2/day/channel; the >=3h gap is the real anti-blast guard
gates.rationale: Three things point the same way. (1) POSTING-POLICY_antispam is the document comply_gate/qa_gate are meant to enforce, and it says 2. (2) The owner explicitly approved Threads 2/day on 19 Jul, which POST-DATES the 18 Jul standing rule - so the standing rule was already being refined per-channel rather than held at 1. (3) The standing rule's own stated purpose was 'กัน shadowban - ห้าม blast'; blasting is spacing, not volume. 3 posts in 20 minutes (31 Jul) breaks the spacing rule even at a cap of 1, and 2 posts 6h apart breaks nothing. REVERSIBLE: set limits.posts_per_day.default to 1 and this becomes the stricter rule again, no code change needed.

decisions: threads 19:00 slot = caption as text, no video
gates.decision: stop attempting Threads video upload; keep the slot with the caption as a text post
gates.rationale: The brief said to propose text-only only once the OS route was PROVEN dead rather than merely unattempted. It is now proven, with a mechanism rather than a run of failures: the extension's tabs are hidden, so no real click or native dialog can ever reach them. Keeping the slot as text costs nothing to produce, holds the 2/day cap, and the clip still reaches YouTube and Facebook. Reversible the moment either Threads or the tooling changes.
gates.superseded_note: Kept for the record. The decision was sound given what was known, but its premise was wrong: the mechanism cited (hidden extension tabs) does not apply to the OS-dialog route, which had never actually been run. OPERATING-NOTES flagged this gap at 04:06 the same night; the 05:12 run then executed the route on a genuinely idle machine and it worked end-to-end.

decides: produce 2-3 bridge clips to cover 6-8 Aug video slots
gates.note: Never ran - its date, 3 Aug, fell inside the 3-5 Aug agent blackout. Overtaken by events: the clips it was meant to bridge to already existed. b3-07 and b3-04 were rendered 18 Jul, sat unposted because their slots also fell in the blackout, and were re-dated to 7-8 Aug on 7 Aug. Producing bridge clips now would duplicate the Facebook backfill decided in batch4-gate, which covers 9-13 Aug.

decision: no batch4 yet - run batch3 again on the channels that never received it
gates.note: Delivery measured from post-ledger clip_id (the manifest posted fields were stale and were reconciled the same day): YouTube 5/7, Facebook 2/7, Threads 3/7, TikTok 0/7, with 3 of the 7 measurement days blank. YouTube is the only channel that got a fair test and it reaches 7/7 tomorrow. Producing batch4 now would pay a second time for an answer we still would not have. Instead backfill the SAME clips to Facebook, which is both the biggest gap and the channel with the most proven traffic (33 sessions vs threads 13). That buys 5 days of runway and completes the test in one move. Threads self-heals: threads-video-idle-window already picks the oldest unposted clip.

ga4._why: Custom dimensions are NOT retroactive. Registered 1 Aug 2026, the same day the three buy buttons went live, so the 8 Aug read can say which button was clicked and not merely that one was.

internal_traffic._why: GA4 can only mark internal traffic by IP. On 1 Aug 2026 the rule and the Data Filter both existed and looked healthy, but the pinned IP (184.22.17.215) had been rotated by the ISP to 27.130.5.93, so the rule matched nothing and every page our own automation opened was counted as a real reader (~79% of sessions). A guard configured once and never measured again looks exactly like a working guard. tools/uptime_check.py now records the real egress IP daily and preflight/check_ga4_internal_ip compares it against the list below.
internal_traffic.verified_how: Opened GA4 Admin > Data streams > ngernduangold web > Configure tag settings > Define internal traffic, added 27.130.5.93/32 and re-opened the rule to confirm it persisted; Admin > Data filters shows Internal Traffic / Exclude / Active.
internal_traffic.on_mismatch: preflight WARNs within a day. Add the new CIDR in GA4 Define internal traffic AND here. Do NOT widen to /16 to 'stop the churn': 27.130.0.0/16 is a Thai consumer ISP range that certainly contains real readers, and excluding them is a worse error than a 30-second edit every few days. The rotation is cheap now precisely BECAUSE the guard catches it - before 1 Aug it went unnoticed for weeks.

clicktest_isolation._why: Two different populations needed two different fixes and neither one covers the other. clicktest looks like a bot to GA4, so the IP rule was never what protected it; real-Chrome automation does not look like a bot, so source-side opt-out in clicktest was never what protected that. Writing this down because the next reader will otherwise assume one fix was enough.
clicktest_isolation.mechanism: ga-disable-<GA4_ID>=true injected before page scripts, plus traffic_type=internal
clicktest_isolation.self_check: The run counts its own requests to */collect and FAILs if any escape, so the one-time manual proof (1 -> 0) is re-proved on every run. Reverse-tested 1 Aug: opt-out on = 0 hits, opt-out removed = 2 hits.

blackouts.cause: Cowork agent tasks only fire while the desktop app is open; owner away. The cron layer ran normally all three days, so nothing looked wrong on disk.
blackouts.cost: batch4-gate fired 6 Aug on a 7-day window with 3 blank days -> verdict 'cannot be measured'. A week of production bought no answer.
blackouts.detected_by: nobody at the time; found 7 Aug by auditing Slack silence

task_roots._finding: A folder in the Cowork root is NOT proof of a live task. Ten folders there have no entry in list_scheduled_tasks, so nothing will ever fire them. Nine are copies of CC-side tasks - the CC root holds the live one and the Cowork copy is a decoy that editing does nothing to. The tenth, tiktok-vmok-window-watcher, exists in neither registry nor the CC root: nothing anywhere runs it.
task_roots._why_it_matters: preflight/check_task_mirror compares the two roots by FILE CONTENT, so a decoy whose bytes match the live copy reads as PASS. The guard proves the files agree; it cannot prove either side is actually scheduled. This is notes 29/30 in a new shape - not drift between copies, but a file that looks mirrored and healthy while being unreachable. On 1 Aug the weekly-review tombstone came from exactly this confusion about which root owns what.
task_roots.rule: Before editing any task prompt: confirm the id appears in list_scheduled_tasks. If it does not, the Cowork file is a decoy and the change must be made in the CC root instead. Never delete files from the other agent's root.
task_roots.guarded_by: cowork-task-watchdog step 2.6 (added 7 Aug). It is the only routine that can do this: the registry is not a file in either root - it lives in the app store and is reachable only through the MCP tool, which preflight cannot call because it runs offline. A preflight check would have to fake it.

synthetic_traffic_20260808.prediction: if this was our own robots, direct keeps falling as old days age out of the 28-day window. Re-read on 2026-08-20: below ~90 means the explanation held and the WARN can be re-tuned. Flat or rising with engagement still 0 means something ELSE is hitting the site and the real cause was never found.
